extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / press-release writers pitching journalists and bloggers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical tips for writing press releases and subject/headlines that attract journalists' and bloggers' attention when they scan high volumes of email. The page lists actionable guidance (only the first tip and introductory note are visible; full article is behind a login).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention-grabbing headline
rubrics_metrics.description: You need a short, catchy headline that will grab somebody’s attention when they’re scanning dozens (or maybe hundreds) of e-mails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at the front page of The New York Times (or any major newspaper or magazine) for examples of great headlines. A headline should 'sell the story'—in this case, your news. If you can’t sell it in your headline, your pitch will likely fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic/annoying subject lines (e.g., 'For Immediate Delete')
rubrics_metrics.description: The article opens by asking whether your releases say 'For Immediate Delete' in the subject line, implying such subject lines drive journalists to hit delete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use unhelpful, clichéd, or attention-repelling subject lines; instead craft a subject that conveys the news value and prompts the recipient to open the message. (Full remedial tips are in the remainder of the article behind login.)
